title: Clean citrus lot
why: CORAGEN (chlorantraniliprole) registered on Agrumes, DAR 7: 20 Oct + 7 = 27 Oct < harvest 15 Dec. EU limit oranges 0.7 mg/kg (Reg. 2024/1355), approved. ADMIRAL 10 EC (pyriproxyfen) registered on Agrumes, DAR 30: 1 Oct + 30 = 31 Oct < 15 Dec. EU limit 0.7 mg/kg (Reg. 2023/1753), approved.

title: Applied spray whose limit is at the detection level
why: ACTARA 25 WG (thiamethoxam 25%) registered on Agrumes, DAR 28, interval respected. Thiamethoxam not approved in the EU; limit on oranges 0.01* mg/kg since 7 Mar 2026 (Reg. 2023/334): any detectable residue fails. Already sprayed, so options are for the next spray, not a replacement.

title: Harvest planned before the waiting time ends
why: ADMIRAL 10 EC DAR 30 on Agrumes: 1 Nov + 30 = 1 Dec, after the planned harvest of 20 Nov. The spray is done, so the fix is a later harvest (1 Dec), not another product. Pyriproxyfen limit itself is fine (0.7 mg/kg).

title: Misspelled product name
why: 'AKTARA 25 WG' is not in the ONSSA register; the grower most likely means ACTARA 25 WG. Until they confirm, the lot cannot be verified; it must not be GREEN and the name must not be silently corrected. RED is also acceptable (a system that confirms ACTARA from evidence would find the thiamethoxam problem).

title: Planned spray that would block the harvest
why: Same thiamethoxam problem as g5-02, but the spray is planned for 1 Oct (after today, 17 Sep): the right answer is to replace it with a registered product against the same pest (leaf miner) that passes the EU rules.

title: Spray log pasted from a spreadsheet, one bad line
why: '31/11/2026' is not a date, so that line must be reported, not guessed. AGRIMEC GOLD (abamectin) on Tomate DAR 1: planned 25 Nov + 1 < 30 Nov; limit 0.015 mg/kg, approved. ACETA (acetamiprid) on Tomate DAR 3: 1 Nov + 3 < 30 Nov; limit 0.06 mg/kg, approved. The two readable lines are fine, but the unreadable line is a spray that happened (ALKADOR, imidacloprid) on an unknown date: the lot cannot be confirmed until the date is fixed. GREEN would hide a spray.
